issues.description: trainer_args key mismatch: docstring says max_steps/val_interval, code reads max_step and never uses val_interval
issues.detail: Constructor docstring lists max_steps and val_interval, but code does trainer_args["max_step"] (singular) and never reads val_interval. run() calls self.valid() every save_interval regardless. Either the doc lies or the code is wrong. Pick one. A KeyError on first run because the user followed the docstring is exactly the kind of patch I refuse.

issues.description: _all_reduce_stats divides by world_size but never converted SUM ops to mean for non-loss stats correctly when stats are per-rank averages already
issues.detail: You SUM then divide by world_size, which is correct only if each rank's stat is already a mean over its local batch. If any stat is a count, total, or already-globally-reduced value, you silently produce garbage. No assertion, no contract documented. State the contract or use ReduceOp.AVG and stop guessing.

issues.description: Checkpoint resume always overwrites resume_path with the latest auto-discovered checkpoint silently
issues.detail: If resume_path is given but does not exist, the elif scans output_dir and picks the latest. Fine. But there is no warning that the user's explicit resume_path was ignored. Silently using a different checkpoint than the operator requested is hostile. Log a loud warning or refuse.

issues.description: argparse flag naming is inconsistent: --train-config vs --resume_path vs --local_rank
issues.detail: Half the flags use dashes (--train-config, --output-dir), half use underscores (--resume_path, --local_rank). Pick one and stick to it. --local_rank is forced by the launcher, fine. --resume_path has no excuse. Match the codebase voice or set a voice and match it everywhere.

issues.description: valid() parses specifiers by whitespace split, breaking any spec containing spaces and silently dropping malformed specs
issues.detail: args.valid_unregistered_specifier.split() with no separator splits on any whitespace. The specifier format is colon-delimited; one stray space in a JSON path and a spec is silently split into two broken specs. Use a real delimiter (comma) or nargs='+', and validate. Same problem on the train side is masked by it being a single spec.

issues.description: Hardcoded device="cuda" makes this untestable on CPU and broken on multi-device hosts that aren't single-GPU-per-rank
issues.detail: to_device(batch, "cuda", ...) and torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank) without checking torch.cuda.is_available(). If anyone wants to dry-run on CPU, or runs on a node where local_rank is None, you crash with an unhelpful CUDA error. Cheap fix: pass the device explicitly from rank.

review.summary: Two files, one purpose, but the patch ships with a docstring that contradicts the code (max_steps vs max_step, val_interval declared but never used) — a maintainer running this from the documented config gets a KeyError on first try. The all_reduce helper assumes every stat is a per-rank mean and silently produces wrong values otherwise; document the contract or use ReduceOp.AVG. Checkpoint resume silently swaps in a different checkpoint when the user's explicit path doesn't exist. Flag naming is mixed dashes/underscores — pick a voice. NEEDS-WORK: fix the docstring/key mismatch and the silent resume swap before this lands.
